question: What developmental stage comes immediately after the egg stage in insects undergoing complete metamorphosis?
explanation: The larval stage follows the egg in complete metamorphosis, serving primarily as the active feeding and growth phase before pupation. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is the larval stage important when controlling vector-borne diseases?

options.A: It is resistant to all insecticides
options.B: It is the final reproductive stage
options.D: It is the main feeding phase where targeted interventions work well

explanation: Targeting vectors during their localized larval development is often more effective than chasing mobile adult insects. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h1)

question: What name is given to the successive developmental moulting phases of growing larvae?
explanation: Larvae grow by shedding their outer cuticle multiple times, with each phase between moults referred to as an instar. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main biological function of the larval stage in most insects?
explanation: Larvae dedicate almost all their energy to consuming nutrients and growing larger to prepare for metamorphosis. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h2)

question: The tumbu fly larva which infests human skin is an example of what condition?
explanation: Myiasis is the infestation of live human or animal tissue by fly larvae. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h3)

question: A patient presents with itchy skin lesions on the feet after walking barefoot on damp soil. Which larval type is responsible?
explanation: Hookworm and Strongyloides larvae live in contaminated soil and actively penetrate bare human skin. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h3)

question: What skin lesion is produced by migrating animal hookworm larvae in cutaneous larva migrans?
explanation: As the larvae crawl through the outer skin layers, they leave behind raised, winding, intensely itchy tracks. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why do furuncular myiasis skin lesions maintain a small central opening?

options.C: To let the larva breathe air
options.D: To allow white blood cells to drain

explanation: The burrowing maggot positions its breathing tubes near the skin opening to breathe while feeding underneath. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h4)

question: Spreading damp clothing on the ground in humid areas can cause infestation by which insect larva?
explanation: Female tumbu flies lay eggs on soil or damp clothing spread outside, and the hatching larvae penetrate skin when garments are worn. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which group faces the highest risk of contracting cutaneous larval infections from contaminated soil?
explanation: Direct skin contact with soil contaminated by animal feces puts barefoot individuals at high risk of larval penetration. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h5)

question: What blood test finding is most commonly associated with tissue-invading parasitic larvae?
explanation: Tissue invasion by parasites typically triggers an elevated white blood cell count dominated by eosinophils. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of taking a detailed travel history when parasitic larvae are suspected?

options.B: To identify the likely source of environmental exposure
options.C: To calculate the exact incubation period

explanation: Knowing where a patient walked or slept helps pinpoint whether the vector originated from soil, clothes, or water. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h6)

question: Applying petroleum jelly to a furuncular myiasis lesion forces the trapped larva to do what?
explanation: Blocking the breathing pore with ointment suffocates the maggot, forcing it to crawl out where it can be extracted safely. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why should you avoid crushing a fly maggot while pulling it out of a skin lesion?

options.B: It triggers a severe local inflammatory reaction
options.C: It causes the larva to multiply

explanation: Leaving larval fragments or body fluids inside the wound provokes intense inflammation and secondary bacterial infection. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h7)

question: What household practice effectively kills tumbu fly eggs hidden in damp laundry?
explanation: High heat from a hot pressing iron destroys any fly eggs or newly hatched larvae lingering in fabric folds. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h8)

question: How do community sanitation programs help reduce vector-borne larval threats?
explanation: Clearing stagnant water removes the necessary aquatic habitat required for mosquito larvae to complete their development. [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h8)
